title: Recovering a Chargeback Shortfall on the Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
Where money charged back by a guest has left a host's Keyturn Host Payout Account short, the marketplace recovers what is owed out of the money the account has since earned rather than invoicing the host for it.

## The handling action

The desk takes the money off the account itself. One recovery books a single new deduction naming the entry it is taken against: the deduction carries the day of the call, the sum taken, the chargeback recovery basis and the statement month the call is made in, and it is booked as a debit so the balance free to be paid out falls by that sum. The earlier entry is left exactly as it stands and the host sees the recovery as its own line on the statement.

## Invoking the recovery

The tool `post_balance_recovery_b10514b8` is unlocked and then called by the agent; it is the desk's own action on the host's account rather than something handed to the host to run.

### Parameters

- `payout_account_id` — the reference number of the Keyturn Host Payout Account the money is taken from, an identifier as returned by the payout account lookup for this host.
- `source_ledger_id` — the reference number of the earlier ledger entry the recovery is taken against, an identifier as returned by the payout ledger lookup for this account.
- `recovery_amount` — the sum taken off the account by this recovery, in USD, given as a positive number rounded half to even to 2 decimal places; there is no empty value and no currency conversion, the account settling in USD throughout.

### Return

A single confirmation sentence in plain text, carrying the reference number of the new deduction, the reference number of the earlier entry it was taken against, and the sum taken in USD to 2 decimal places. The presence of that deduction reference is what indicates the money has been taken off the account.

## Points of judgement

**Is the host invoiced for the shortfall?** No. What is owed is recovered out of the money the account has since earned.

**Is the earlier entry altered?** No. It is left exactly as it stands, and the recovery appears as its own line on the statement.
